what: Standing low-poly figure stacked from basic shapes (height = …plate height ÷ 1.12) is drawn at half resolution so the pixels show, set up in a PS2 style: flat shading per face, sky-ground hemisphere light + upper-left sunlight. The chest swells 1.8% on a 1.7rad/s cycle and the upper body sways sideways by 1.8% of its height on a .75rad cycle. With spin: scroll, it turns −180°→180° as the plate passes from the bottom to the top of the screen (.12 per frame). Otherwise the body turns ±.6rad according to how far the cursor is from the screen center (.05 per frame).

options.spin: With scroll, it turns once around on scroll, otherwise it spins following the cursor
options.pixel: Drawing resolution scale, default .5 (retro console style) — also set image-rendering: pixelated in the element css
options.look: If smooth, render crisply at device resolution
options.Color: Skin, top, pants, shoe and hair colors are mixed from the theme variables (--site-sun·--kf-ink-soft·--kf-contrast-bg·--kf-bg·--kf-accent)

from.where: poly.js — first-page black panel intro (spin: scroll) · About page hero (follows the cursor). Original PolyAvatar: scanned-person glb, ps2 pixel .5, breathing shader 1.7·.75, scroll (clamp − .5)×2π lerp .12, cursor ×.6 lerp .05

note: The original is a human scan model (glb) — the part substitutes a basic-shape figure with the same height and silhouette ratio. To use a model file, load it with GLTFLoader instead of figure() and apply the same material. The shader compiles when attached
